A1.justification: Both PDFs describe miniF2F-Dafny and the same 488-problem benchmark. Their complete text, tables, figures, and Appendices A–B are readable and can be matched despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: Section 3 and Table 1 report original Dafny empty-proof and 12-model evaluations. Appendix A includes generated proof examples.

after.justification: Section 4 and Table 2 report Dafny, seven-model, and Lean grind evaluations. Section 3.4 also reports a manual verification study covering 14 problems.

M1.justification: The supplied mathematical context expands from 108 to 174 library lemmas, adding rational-field facts and broader support for powers and finite sums. This changes available proof-building blocks, while the proof-generation/refinement procedure, specification validator, and Appendix B prompts remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same 488 mathematical problems, split into 244 test and 244 validation problems, with unchanged domain coverage. The Lean comparison and manual study use corresponding problems or subsets of this existing coverage.

E2.justification: V2 Table 2 adds Lean grind and removes five evaluated LLMs from v1 Table 1: Claude Sonnet 3.7, DeepSeek V3.1, Llama 4 Maverick 17B, GPT-OSS 120B, and Qwen 3 235B A22B. The LLM comparison therefore contracts from twelve models to seven.

E3.justification: V2 revises the supplied background library, adds testing with grind on 244 Lean problems, and introduces manual checking of 14 randomly selected problems. Sonnet 4's reported attempted-problem count changes from 243 to 244. Temperature, response-token limit, and three correction iterations are retained; the independent-trajectory wording clarifies the existing four-attempt setup.

E4.justification: New Section 3.4 tests library sufficiency and translation through manual proofs of 14 problems involving integer sums, integer products, and logarithms. The existing error-analysis categories and worked proof cases, including both Appendix A solutions, are retained.

E5.justification: The stated empty-proof verification repetition count decreases from five attempts to four. V2 explicitly describes independent LLM trajectories and removes v1's footnote identifying partial-evaluation rates as projected. Neither version reports confidence intervals, variances, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Dafny's test result changes from 99/244 (40.6%) to 95/244 (38.9%), and validation from 109/244 (44.7%) to 106/244 (43.4%). V2 adds grind's 79/244 (32.4%) and 14/14 manual successes, while removing five LLM result sets. All retained LLM percentages, including the best 55.7%, are unchanged. Revised library and verification-attempt settings prevent interpreting the baseline difference as a same-setting performance decline.

T1.justification: The reported axiomatic foundation substantially expands, including integer-power support, bounds on pi, absolute-value inequalities, broader finite-sum properties, and ten rational-field lemmas. Powers grow from 8 to 28 lemmas and sequences from 8 to 32. Existing displayed definitions and Appendix A proofs are unchanged; the new manual study supplies no formal consistency proof.

C1.justification: The first-translation and LLM/automation division-of-labor contributions remain. V2 narrows the evaluated-model claim from twelve to seven, revises the automation range from 40–45% to 39–44%, and adds an explicit introductory claim of stronger automation than Lean grind. The best reported success rate remains 55.7%.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the grind comparison as evidence that many miniF2F problems are routine and the manual proofs as evidence of soundness and preserved translation semantics. It also shifts Qwen from the families described as having stronger Dafny familiarity to those with limited knowledge. Existing brittleness and incomplete-library limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 clarifies conversation construction for independent trajectories and explicitly connects it to the retained prompts. It reports 81 definitions in 283 lines, versus the earlier 300-line description, and updates the library inventory to 174 lemmas in 938 lines. Dafny version, Bedrock integration, appendix prompts, and benchmark repository access remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The introduction substantially repositions the benchmark within the mathematics/software-verification and interactive/auto-active divide, summarized in new Table 1. Added literature covers CLEVER, Verina, VerifyThis, other auto-active tools, industrial applications, Dafny interactive proof modes, Velvet, and Strata. Related work also adds Seed-Prover 1.5 and Numina-Lean Agent.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten around the verification-paradigm divide. A substantial Dafny-language background section precedes the benchmark description, and a soundness subsection and impact statement are added. Authorship is updated. The appendix proofs and prompts retain their substantive wording.

P2.justification: V2 substantially reformats the title, headers, typography, captions, and tables. It adds the benchmark-landscape table and a simple Dafny-method figure, restructures and relocates the results table, and reflows retained figures. Appendices change from two-column presentation to full-width listings across pages.

improvement.justification: V2 provides clearer exposition, broader research context, and a useful Lean comparison. However, Table 2 lists every retained model at 244 problems while Section 4.2 still describes partial evaluation; Sonnet 4 retains its previously projected percentages despite its revised count. The relationship between unchanged LLM scores and revised library/baseline conditions is unexplained. The manual study demonstrates provability but does not establish the asserted axiomatization soundness. These reporting and evidential concerns prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
